body.statement: For sample sizes in the deterministic eventual regime \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}T_n(P)\ge T_0\), the sets \(\mathcal C_n(a)\) are intervals, and \(\Pr_P\{\theta(a)\in\mathcal C_n(a)\text{ for all }a\in J\}\to1-\alpha\) uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\). The image construction in \(\texttt{def:crossing-set}\) is therefore an eventual-regime simultaneous \((1-\alpha)\)-level confidence set for \(\tau_{\zeta}\) for every fixed \(\zeta\), including the empty and all-domain conventions.
body.justification: Joint LR calibration should report the scientifically interpretable crossing doses and the whole curve with one common coverage event.
body.gap: Doss (2026) reports pointwise LR intervals in the nurse-staffing application; the proposition uses a genuinely simultaneous LR critical value and a coverage-preserving inverse map.
body.consumer: AHA/CMS analysts can report the nurse-hours level at which the readmission profile crosses a policy-relevant threshold with simultaneous uncertainty.

obligation.what_is_open: The deterministic interval and crossing-set inversion is proved, but its nominal limiting coverage remains the unresolved probability statement in feasible calibration.
obligation.obstruction: Convexity and set-image arguments preserve the coverage of the common LR event; they cannot establish that the current critical value has asymptotic probability one minus the nominal error.
obligation.attempted: The constrained value function was shown convex, the band event was identified exactly with the supremum event, and the true monotone curve was shown to map to its threshold crossing under all endpoint conventions.
